brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: compact single-cell tower with top cover, dressed with heap-screws, heap-nuts and tweezers props; check_build clear
requirements.requirement: for a workbench (small-footprint bench storage, staged with workshop small parts)

finish.summary: Two-storey half-n tower with one drawer per storey (both opened), capped faces, top cover, locked joints, and workshop props (screws, nuts, tweezers) to show bench use. Verified: check clear, mesh clear.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

Half-n and half-s take any drawer style; half-e and half-w take a slide, swing or long drawer (find_sockets offers those once the half base is on). No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
